key_insight: The classical 2-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm stabilizes in at most 5(n−1) rounds, improving the prior O(n log n) bound and matching the known linear lower bound up to a constant factor.
engineering_relevance: This gives sharper worst-case runtime guarantees for graph refinement methods used in graph isomorphism pipelines and related combinatorial ML or algebraic tools.
method: Proves a new linear upper bound for the 2-dimensional WL refinement process.
Extends the analysis to k-dimensional WL for all k≥3, yielding O(n^(k−1)/(k−2)! + n^(k−2)) iterations.
Uses arguments that also apply to a broader class of tuple-coloring sequences.
evidence_signal: The paper’s main evidence is a theoretical convergence bound: 5(n−1) iterations for the classical case, plus improved asymptotic bounds for higher dimensions.
watch_item: The result is a worst-case iteration bound, so practical speedups may be smaller and depend on graph structure and implementation details.
paper_title: The Classical Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm Stabilizes in $O(n)$ Rounds
